Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has an inlet chiller in front of the compressor. In warm weather it cools the intake air down to a fixed set temperature. Over this ambient range the gas turbine stays below the rated limit of its generator. The plant has no inlet anti-icing system. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. The chiller set temperature is about 20 degC; the chiller runs whenever ambient temperature is above it.

"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling, inlet_chilling is an inlet chiller. "response_beyond" compares how net output responds to ambient temperature beyond at_c with how it responds elsewhere in the range: weaker = same direction but a clearly smaller change per degC; near_zero = output barely changes with ambient temperature; opposite = output changes in the opposite direction; same_or_stronger = same direction and at least as large a change per degC.
